item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission examined WA Health's ability to manage procurement fraud and corruption risks following an investigation of a hospital facilities manager.
item.support: A subsequent Commission review of WA Health's capacity to deal with its fraud and corruption risks in procurement

item.text: The Commission found that weak financial controls and supervision had enabled corrupt conduct to remain undetected for six years.
item.support: Wickramasinghe's conduct went undetected for six years because of poor financial controls and poor supervision of him.

item.text: It concluded that these weaknesses reflected a systemic failure across WA Health to manage procurement fraud and corruption risks.
item.support: It was a symptom of systemic failure to manage fraud and corruption risks in procurement across WA Health.

item.text: Its five recommendations covered risk assessment, compliance and transparency, internal audit, staff training, conflicts of interest, gifts and outside employment.
item.support: In that context, the Commission makes the following five recommendations to WA Health

item.quote: WA Health has limited capacity to effectively manage conflicts of interest, gifts and benefits and outside employment.
There is no systematic training in recognising and reporting fraud and corruption for WA Health staff engaged in procurement.
